authors.stance_zh: 李永晶的立场是认识论的：不急于回答「日本是什么」，而先问「我们为何这样问」。他把黄遵宪、戴季陶、本尼迪克特串成一条镜链，指出每一次知日都是一次自我定位；因此「新日本论」之新，在于把提问者放回问题之中。
authors.stance_en: Li's stance is epistemological: rather than answer what Japan is, he asks why we ask it that way. Huang, Dai and Benedict form a mirror-chain in which every knowing of Japan is a self-positioning; the newness of a new Japan-ology lies in putting the asker back inside the question.
authors.why_now_zh: 在中日关系与民族情绪反复摆动的当下，他提供的是降温的读法：把对日本的判断转成对自己的检视。这与本批「甲 思想史」一线正好同频。
authors.why_now_en: At a moment when Sino-Japanese relations and national sentiment swing repeatedly, he offers a cooling reading: turn judgement of Japan into examination of the self, in tune with the batch's intellectual-history axis.

authors.why_now_en: In an age that demands preservation, restoration and digitisation, he reminds us that some beauty exists only in erasure, giving the batch's theme a contemporary pivot.

authors.stance_zh: 漱石的立场是「非人情」：不以利害与情感介入世界，而以诗画之眼观照。但这并非逃避，他把最锋利的社会批评留在俏皮话里，把最深的自我解剖留在病榻上。
authors.stance_en: Soseki's stance is disinterestedness: not interest or sentiment but a poet's and painter's eye. It is no escape: his sharpest social criticism hides in wit, his deepest self-dissection on the sickbed.
authors.why_now_zh: 当「内耗」成为日常词，漱石的病榻写作提供了一种更诚实的自我技术：把病写下来，而不是把病浪漫化。
authors.why_now_en: When burnout is everyday vocabulary, Soseki's sickbed writing offers an honester technology of the self: write the illness down rather than romanticise it.

authors.why_now_en: When the Anthropocene is written in capitals, Tsing insists on concrete patches and multispecies collaboration.

authors.stance_zh: 发展不是中性援助，而是话语权力；世界不止一个，设计可以参与生成多元宇宙。
authors.stance_en: Development is not neutral aid but discursive power; there is more than one world, and design can participate in making pluriverses.
authors.why_now_zh: 当「另一种可能」成为全球口号，Escobar 给出后发展与多元宇宙的政治本体论。
authors.why_now_en: When 'another possible' becomes a global slogan, Escobar supplies the political ontology of post-development and the pluriverse.
